evidence: paper: X_a = 4/\Lambda, \qquad X_R = 110 (C P_*)^{10}, \qquad x = X/X_R, \qquad X_h = X_R e^{-5}, \qquad f = (1+\eta^2)^{-1}.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. All five defining equations appear as Lean definitions. X_a = 4/Λ is `NominalConeAssembly.activeLeft W = 4 / W.axis.scale`; X_R = 110(CP_*)^10 is `matchingRadius F C = resetRadius Xi C F.data.core.P` with `Xi = 110` and `resetRadius Xi C P = Xi * (C*P)^10` (the paper's P_* is `F.data.core.P`, the paper's C is the amplitude normalization); X_h = X_R e^{-5} is `matchRadius = matchingRadius * matchFraction` with `matchFraction = Real.exp (-5)`; f = (1+η²)^{-1} is `OutgoingSchedule.shape eta = (1 + eta^2)⁻¹`. For x = X/X_R the division is literal in the repository: `Controls.radius c = matchingRadius F A.normalization` is X_R, and `Controls.E p = c.normalizedE (p.1 / c.radius, p.2)`, `Controls.U p = c.normalizedU (p.1 / c.radius, p.2)` — the physical field at radius X evaluated as the normalized field at x = X / X_R (NominalProfile.lean:661-663). The only notational point is that Lean has no standalone abbreviation `x`: the rescaling lives in the arguments, written as the division X/X_R in `Controls.E`/`Controls.U` and as the inverse substitution X = X_R·x in the constructors `preparedE`/`preparedU`. Equivalent as a change of variable; nothing in the five constants differs.
